newsitem.title: USA: Tampa Bay, Fla., Bucs agree to revised lease.
newsitem.headline: Tampa Bay, Fla., Bucs agree to revised lease.

text.p: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers agreed to give up a lease provision that prompted a judge to reject validation of $204.5 million of stadium bonds, city and Hillsborough County officials said.

The original lease with the Tampa Sports Authority would have given the team the first $2 million of annual revenues from non-Bucs events at the stadium. A revised agreement calls for the team to split the money with the sports authority.

Last month, Hillsborough County Circuit Judge Sam Pendino refused to validate the sports authority's stadium tax-exempt bond issue, ruling that the $2 million payment made the stadium a project for mainly private benefit.
Pendino said he could approve the bonds if the $2 million provision was eliminated.
In the meantime, former Tampa Mayor Bill Poe, who had sued to block the bond issue, appealed to the Florida Supreme Court. That removed the case from Pendino's jurisdiction.
The Florida Supreme Court court scheduled a hearing on May 7 and is expected to rule before recessing in July.

Hillsborough County voters approved a sales tax increase in September to fund school and public safety projects and the stadium. The Sports Authority bond issue was planned for November but has been delayed by the legal action.

Stadium construction began last fall with $19.5 million of proceeds from the sale of sports authority land. That money is running out, the the authority has asked Hillsborough County to partly back a $10 million loan to continue construction until the court rules.
The county scheduled a hearing on the request Wednesday and could rule later this week.
